perspective: Adversarial verification of renewal, reappointment, and semester-rollover semantics against all three interview transcripts and all three derived Markdown artifacts.

findings.claim: Renewal/reappointment is not automatic. Faculty must confirm or edit the proposed appointment each cycle, especially chartfield/funding data.
evidence: Call with Mayra Morfin (1).docx:79-86 — chartfield may change; Mayra says they do not want automatic renewals and need faculty confirmation.
Call with Mayra Morfin (1).docx:44-52 — prior-semester data is sent as a snippet and faculty are asked for changes; new appointments require the full fields.
mayra_student_hiring_flow.md:8-12, 50-53 — derived summary matches the transcript, but remains provisional.
findings.risk: A default-copy or silent renewal could carry forward an invalid funding source and misassign responsibility to Finance.
findings.recommendation: Model renewal as an explicit faculty-confirmation event with confirmed, edited, and outstanding states; never treat copied data as approval.

findings.claim: The renewal input is a prior-semester snippet, not a new blank request; faculty review the copied values and can edit them.
evidence: Call with Mayra Morfin (1).docx:44-46 — Mayra uses the previous semester spreadsheet and sends a snippet asking whether students are renewing and for changes.
mayra_student_hiring_flow.md:51-53 — renewal_snippet followed by faculty_confirm.
findings.risk: Treating the snippet as authoritative would hide changed job codes, hours, rates, or chartfields.
findings.recommendation: Persist both the prior-semester snapshot and the faculty-confirmed next-semester values.

findings.claim: Reappointments use existing Oracle person data; the new-hire Banner/pending-worker path is a distinct branch.
evidence: HR App (1).docx:568-578 — Laura says reappointments already have the information in Oracle; new hires require pending-worker entry, Banner address lookup, DOB, gender, and phone.
HR App (1).docx:412-421 — Laura contrasts reappointment address retrieval from Oracle with new-student lookup in Banner.
student_hiring_pipeline.md:40-42 — D1/D2 new-hire detour and D3 reappointment skip.
findings.risk: Applying new-hire collection requirements to reappointments creates unnecessary work; applying the reappointment shortcut to new hires omits required identity data.
findings.recommendation: Branch explicitly on appointment/person status and retain the branch decision in the record.

findings.claim: For spring, Mayra copies fall data into the spring tab; unchanged rows remain done/no-action, while highlighted changed rows require processing.
evidence: HR App (1).docx:962-978 — most appointments span nine months; Mayra copies data to the spring tab, highlights changes, and unchanged rows stay blue with no Laura action.
HR App (1).docx:986-987 — changed spring assignments require the process, including foreign-principal, letter, and entry/change work.
student_hiring_pipeline.md:43-45 — D5 records the copy-over and highlighted-change behavior.
findings.risk: A bulk spring rollover that reprocesses every copied row creates needless work; one that processes none misses changed assignments.
findings.recommendation: Implement row-level no-change versus changed classification; only changed rows create a new work item, while preserving the copied prior-semester values.

findings.claim: A post-completion change is not an in-place silent edit: it requires a tracked request, a new/revised offer-letter step, and an Oracle amendment; Finance may need revised funding data.
evidence: HR App (1).docx:780-851 — Laura describes changing completed TA/RA appointments; she needs a new offer letter and Oracle amendment, with Mayra as the intake path.
HR App (1).docx:1023-1053 — changed job/funding data must be visible to Daisy/Jamie and the request history must be retained for audit.
Call with Mayra Morfin (1).docx:214-226 — late job-code changes occur after onboarding and overwrite must be restricted.
daisy_finance_stage.md:19-24, 37-46 — funding problems loop through update and re-verification.
findings.risk: Overwriting the current row destroys audit history and can leave HR, Oracle, and Finance out of sync.
findings.recommendation: Represent changes as linked revisions/requests with requester, confirmation/approval state, effective semester, and downstream completion state.

findings.claim: Finance verifies chartfields and may require a new account or changed chartfield; the appointment is not financially complete merely because HR copied or confirmed the row.
evidence: Call with Mayra Morfin (1).docx:444-462 — chartfields may be prefilled, but Finance checks distributions and account use.
Call with Daisy Matos.docx:1022-1049 — Finance verifies chartfield, discusses changes when funds are unavailable, updates the worksheet, and records completion/date/initials.
daisy_finance_stage.md:17-31, 67-80 — derived finance loop and active-monitoring semantics.
findings.risk: Treating faculty confirmation as sufficient financial validation can propagate stale or unfunded chartfields.
findings.recommendation: Keep faculty confirmation and Finance verification as separate lifecycle events.

findings.claim: The derived artifacts are broadly accurate but overstate or normalize several points that are only proposals or assumptions.
evidence: mayra_student_hiring_flow.md:10 — 'confirmation is required every time' is directionally supported, but the transcript does not define the exact confirmation protocol or deadline.

mayra_student_hiring_flow.md:25-31 and 76-80 — Laura/Daisy ordering and some late-change/default-account edges are explicitly marked assumed or second-hand, so they must not be treated as primary authority.

student_hiring_pipeline.md:43-45 and 97-114 — 'only highlighted rows re-enter the pipeline' is a useful derived interpretation, but the transcript says changed rows require action rather than defining a formal pipeline reset.
daisy_finance_stage.md:26-31 and 101-106 — exact post-entry status is unresolved ('page', probably 'paid'), and the grad-student/fringe/summer applicability remains open.
Call with Mayra Morfin (1).docx:116-124 — 'auto-approve for most' is Ian's proposal, not confirmed policy.
findings.risk: A summary-level state machine could accidentally turn design proposals, assumptions, or unclear labels into enforced policy.
findings.recommendation: Keep transcript evidence, corroborated behavior, derived interpretation, and design proposal in separate fields; do not implement 'auto-approve', exact statuses, or full reset semantics without owner confirmation.

missing_or_ambiguous: Whether a faculty confirmation is required for every copied row, including unchanged rows, or whether unchanged rows are implicitly accepted after a defined deadline.
Exact system status/state names for renewal confirmation, changed-row processing, Finance completion, and the unclear Daisy status ('page', probably 'paid').
Whether changed spring rows always repeat foreign-principal screening or only the offer-letter/Oracle amendment path; Laura describes the whole process but does not specify exceptions.
Whether a faculty-confirmed chartfield is a hard prerequisite before Finance verification or merely an input to Finance review.
What happens when faculty never respond: deadline, escalation, non-renewal, or carry-forward behavior is not defined.

Whether renewal is per student, per assignment, or per supervisor request in the data model; the Laura transcript confirms one student can have multiple Oracle assignments, but does not define renewal identity rules.
